title: A New Paradigm of Social Support: Circles of Support in Social Service Centers as a Tool for Systemic Change in Poland
content: This study examines the feasibility of implementing circles of support for persons with disabilities within social service centers in Poland as a systemic solution promoting community-based support. Using action research methodology, the authors developed and tested the model in two diverse municipalities, analyzing legal, financial, and organizational dimensions. Results demonstrate that circles of support are fully legally permissible and cost-effective, with approximate annual costs per participant comparable across different organizational models. Key barriers include limited financial and human resources, particularly in rural areas. Nevertheless, the model aligns with deinstitutionalization policies and demonstrates significant potential to enhance the social inclusion, independence, and quality of life of people with disabilities. The study underlines the necessity of sustainable funding, comprehensive staff training, and integration of formal and informal support systems. Findings contribute to the growing body of evidence supporting localized, personalized disability services and offer practical guidance for scaling up circles of support nationwide.
